package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest version at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: DEFENSOR ID is a banking Trojan distributed via the official Google Play Store. It is designed to steal sensitive information from victims, including bank account credentials, cryptocurrency wallet private keys, and two-factor authentication codes. The app masquerades as a legitimate security or banking tool but performs credential theft and exfiltration, violating user trust and platform policies.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after app launch and user interaction)
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (Android app, likely in MainActivity or background service)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses accessibility services to monitor user input, captures banking credentials and two-factor authentication codes, searches for cryptocurrency wallet keys, and exfiltrates all collected data to a remote command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app requests excessive permissions unrelated to its stated purpose, monitors user input, intercepts SMS messages, and exfiltrates sensitive data to an external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate banking or security app should not capture user credentials, intercept SMS 2FA codes, or search for private keys, nor should it send such data to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility services may be used by legitimate apps for assisting users with disabilities, but not for credential theft.
key_indicators: Abuse of accessibility services for credential harvesting
Interception of SMS messages for 2FA code theft
Searching for and exfiltrating cryptocurrency wallet keys
Network communication with external C2 server

attack_chain.action: User installs DEFENSOR ID from the Google Play Store, granting requested permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is launched and begins malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: App abuses accessibility services to monitor user input and capture credentials.
App intercepts SMS messages to steal two-factor authentication codes.
App searches device storage for cryptocurrency wallet private keys.
All harvested data is exfiltrated to a remote command-and-control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Abuse of Android accessibility services to monitor user input
Interception of SMS messages for 2FA code theft
Unusual file system access patterns searching for wallet keys
Exfiltration of sensitive data to external servers
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml requesting ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, READ_SMS, and broad storage permissions
App package name and certificate not matching known legitimate banking/security apps
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains or IPs associated with banking trojans
Unencrypted HTTP POST requests containing credential or wallet data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps requesting excessive permissions (especially accessibility and SMS), analyze runtime behavior for credential harvesting and exfiltration, inspect network traffic for suspicious outbound connections, and flag apps that search for wallet files or intercept 2FA codes. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify code patterns typical of banking trojans.
